explanation: Landscape preservation involves protecting large geographic areas, which benefits multiple wildlife species sharing that space rather than just a single target species. An important factor in landscape ecology is the edge effect. The border or edge of a habitat patch (such as a forest edge) exhibits environmental conditions different from the interior. Because edges reduce the amount of typical, stable interior habitat, they can cause significant reductions in population sizes. When habitat fragmentation occurs, creating smaller patches increases the overall proportion of the habitat subjected to these edge effects.

opts: The migration of species from marine to freshwater ecosystems
The different environmental conditions found at the border of a habitat patch compared to its interior
The rapid recycling of nutrients in tropical rainforest soils
The positive feedback loop driving overexploitation

questions.q: How does habitat fragmentation into smaller patches affect organisms in relation to the edge effect?
opts: It eliminates the edge effect entirely.
It increases the proportion of individuals subjected to the edge effect, reducing typical interior habitat.
It increases the overall carrying capacity of the ecosystem.
It forces species to undergo photorespiration.
